Myths on Clay tells the ancient myths in the style of Greek black-figure vase painting, one story at a time, in the order the Greeks told them.
Sources: Hesiod's Theogony and Works and Days, the Homeric Hymns, Apollodorus' Library, Ovid's Metamorphoses.
Narrated by Matías.

griegas-01-origen.gancho: Before the gods, before the heroes and the monsters, there was nothing but Chaos. This is how the Greek world was born: Gaia and Uranus, the Titans, Cronus swallowing his own children, the hidden baby Zeus, and the ten-year war that put the Olympians on the throne.

griegas-02-prometeo.gancho: Zeus ruled from Olympus, but humans were left cold and helpless. One Titan decided to defy the king of the gods. This is the story of Prometheus: the trick at Mecone, the stolen fire hidden in a fennel stalk, and the terrible punishment in the Caucasus.
